paper.title: Class prediction for high-dimensional class-imbalanced data
paper.citation: Blagus R, Lusa L. Class prediction for high-dimensional class-imbalanced data. BMC Bioinformatics 11:523 (2010)

simulation.what: Each simulated data set is a training set of 80 and separate test sets drawn from the same distributions, with round(80 k1train) Class 1 samples; the paper splits 100 samples into 80 and 20.
Random seeds: one per setting and replicate (from the setting's name); the paper's seeds are not given.

Replicates: 1,000 per setting, as in the paper, for the null case at p = 40 and the alternative case at p = 1000 (Figs 1 and 5's first column, Additional files 1, 3 and 11); 500 for every other setting and 200 for Additional file 6 and the hypothesis tests (compute budget). The tolerance uses our replicate count and the paper's.
Ties: DLDA and DQDA give ties to Class 1 (as sma::stat.diag.da); k-NN breaks ties at random (class::knn); PLR breaks ties at 0.5 at random (as stated).
RF: randomForest defaults (500 trees, mtry = sqrt(p)) with classwt = the training class proportions, as stated; RF-THR classifies as Class 1 when the vote share exceeds k1train.
SVM: e1071::svm, linear kernel, scale = FALSE, class.weights = the training class proportions (as stated) and the default cost 1 (not stated).
PAM: pamr.train with its default 30 thresholds; the largest threshold with the smallest training error (as stated).
PLR: stepPlr::plr with lambda = 1 (as stated), Class 1 coded 1.

AUC scores: share of neighbour votes (k-NN), difference of the two discriminants (DLDA, DQDA), vote share (RF), decision value (SVM), posterior (PAM), fitted probability (PLR). The paper says only that Hmisc was used.

A predictive value has no value in a replicate whose denominator is 0 (PV1 when PA1 = 0 and PA2 = 1). Means are over the replicates where the value exists; a cell the paper prints as NA or NaN counts as equal when some of our replicates have no value.

corrections.what: Over-sampling draws the max(n1, n2) - min(n1, n2) replicated minority samples with replacement; down-sizing keeps min(n1, n2) majority samples drawn without replacement.
MultDS: 101 down-sized sets, t-test selection of 40 variables inside each, majority vote (as stated). At k1train = 0.5 no sample is left out, so all 101 classifiers are the same.
Variable centering is applied to the training set the classifier is fitted on (after over- or down-sizing, inside each MultDS set) and to the test set separately.
Predictive values use the original training proportion (k1train), also after a correction.

er.what: Data: the BRB-ArrayTools project of Sotiriou et al. (2003) in the NCI BRB data archive; its RawData, ProcessedLog and FilteredAndNormalizedLog arrays are identical (median-centred log ratios); missing values set to 0, as stated.

Each of the 500 draws per design takes the training samples and 20 test samples per class without replacement from the ER+ and ER- tumours; class 1 is ER+; predictive values use the training proportion of ER+.
Fig. 6 and Additional file 12 draw the designs at their ER+ share (50, 66.7, 80, 85.7, 90% with 5 ER-; 50, 66.7, 75, 81.8% with 10 ER-); each plotted point is matched to the nearest design.
er.sensitivity: The nearest design is at least 4 points of ER+ share away from the next; a wrong match would put a point 5 or more points off in x.

figure_values.what: Published values are read from the vector figures: the paper's markers and the supplements' polyline vertices, mapped through each panel's tick marks (largest tick-fit residual below 0.0002 in y); points within 0.0005 of ours count as equal for reading error.

Monte Carlo tolerance: |ours - paper| <= printed + z sqrt(se_ours^2 + se_paper^2), se = SD / sqrt(replicates), with the paper's SD where printed and ours otherwise, the paper's 1,000 (500 for the breast cancer data) replicates, and z the Bonferroni value for a 5% chance of any false miss in the item.

mu_grid.what: The mu2 grid of Fig. 4 is 0, 0.1, ..., 2.0 and 3, read from the figure's markers; Methods gives 0.1, 0.2, ..., 1.9, 2, 3 and Results 0, 0.25, ..., 2, 2.5, 3.
mu_grid.sensitivity: All 22 plotted x positions fall within 0.0002 of this grid; neither printed grid fits them (0.25 steps would put 13 of the 22 points off the grid).

pi.what: Prediction-interval ends are our 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles over replicates (R's quantile type 7); with a 20-sample test set they move in steps of 0.05, and they count as equal within one step.

claims.what: Words such as 'about' are read as within 0.05; each claim's reading is stated in its fields and recomputed from the paper's own values first (text.arithmetic).

fig12.summary: (1) SVM: the paper gives no cost, and its class weights ('the proportion of samples from each class') leave the direction open. With the default cost 1 our SVM is less biased than the paper's in the simulations (Additional file 3, k1train 0.1: PA1 {svm_af3_ours} against 0.03; there the weights change nothing at cost 1). A smaller cost with the stated weights brings Additional file 3 back (cost 0.1: {svm_c01_af3}; 0.03: {svm_c003_af3}) but sends the null case of Fig. 2 to 0 (cost 0.1: {svm_c01_null} against 0.038). On the breast cancer data the stated weights go the wrong way (20 ER+ / 5 ER-, PA ER-: {svm_prop_er} at cost 1 against 0.6); weights inverse to the class sizes with cost 0.1 give {svm_inv_er} there but {svm_inv_er45} at 45 ER+ / 5 ER- (paper 0.49). Weights taken from the original rather than the over-sampled training set change nothing ({svm_over_w}). No cost and weighting of the grid fits all of them. (2) PAM without correction: our PAM is slightly more biased than the paper's near balance in the null case (Fig. 1, k1train 0.45: PA1 {pt_null_a} against 0.27) and at 45 ER+ / 5 ER- (PA ER- {pt_er_a} against 0.53). The paper says the threshold was the one with the smallest training error, not which one of the ties. The smallest tied threshold gives {pt_null_s} and {pt_er_s}; 10-fold CV {pt_null_cv} and {pt_er_cv}; equal class priors {pt_null_e} and {pt_er_e}. None fits both. Without variable selection (Additional file 6) the difference runs the other way: the paper's PAM puts nearly every sample in the majority class (k1train 0.2: PA {pt_af6_p}), ours less so ({pt_af6_a}). (3) Values near 0 or 1: a few points where our replicates are all or nearly all 0 or 1, so the Monte Carlo tolerance is close to 0, and the paper's values differ from ours by less than 0.003.

nocenter.summary: p = 40 and pDE = p: the paper says the samples were centred, and with centring our minority-class PA is far below the paper's where 20 of 40 or all of the variables differ ({nc_fig3_c} of {nc_fig3_cn} such points of Fig. 3 match, {nc_af4_c} of {nc_af4_n} of Additional file 4, {nc_af5_c} of {nc_af5_n} of Additional file 5). Centring the samples over 40 variables of which half or all are shifted removes most of the signal. Rerunning these settings without centring (200 replicates) matches {nc_fig3} of {nc_fig3_n} points of Fig. 3, {nc_af4} of {nc_af4_n} of Additional file 4 and {nc_af5} of {nc_af5_n} of Additional file 5; what still misses is the SVM, PAM at pDE = p, and the k1train = 0.95 end at pDE = 20, where the paper's PA1 is a little lower than either of our runs. Our run keeps the stated centring.

fig5.summary: (1) Over-sampling, overall PA: Fig. 5's over-sampling PA is the PA of a test set as imbalanced as the training set (k1 PA1 + (1 - k1) PA2 from our class-specific means: {ot_fig5_i} of {ot_fig5_n} points match, against {ot_fig5_b} for the balanced test set the caption implies), while Additional file 8, which repeats the panel for all classifiers, uses the balanced test set ({ot_af8_b} of {ot_af8_n} against {ot_af8_i}). The two figures disagree; we compare with the balanced test set. (2) Over-sampling, order of selection: with variables selected on the original training set and the classifier fitted on the over-sampled one, DLDA's and DQDA's PA at k1train 0.2 is {ord_dlda_b} and {ord_dqda_b} (paper: {ord_dlda_p}, {ord_dqda_p}); selecting on the over-sampled set, which the Methods describe and our run does, gives {ord_dlda_a} and {ord_dqda_a}. The k-NN classifiers move little either way (3-NN {ord_3nn_a} / {ord_3nn_b}). (3) Values near 0 or 1: a few points where our replicates are all or nearly all 0 or 1, so the Monte Carlo tolerance is close to 0, and the paper's values differ from ours by less than 0.003.

With the default cost 1 our SVM is less biased than the paper's in the simulations (Additional file 3, k1train 0.1: PA1 {svm_af3_ours} against 0.03; there the weights change nothing at cost 1). er_pi.summary: Prediction intervals: a few interval ends miss by two steps of 0.05, nearly all lower ends at the smallest training sets ({pi_fig6} of {pi_fig6_n} ends of Fig. 6 and {pi_af12} of {pi_af12_n} of Additional file 12 match). The lower 2.5th percentile of 500 draws rests on its 13 lowest values, which the paper's draws (unknown seeds) and ours place differently. Other interval definitions fit worse: mean -/+ 1.96 SD matches {pi_fig6_norm} and {pi_af12_norm}, 5th and 95th percentiles {pi_fig6_q90} and {pi_af12_q90}.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The intervals are 90% (5th and 95th percentiles)
hypotheses.test: compare.py: fig6.pi.q90, af12.q90

pi_multds.summary: MultDS at 45 ER+ / 5 ER-: our lower ER+ interval limits sit at 0.60 for most classifiers, one 0.05 step below the paper's 0.65, so 'above 0.60' fails by one step; the ER- half of the statement is not supported by the paper's own Additional file 12 either. The interval ends move in steps of 0.05 and rest on the lowest 13 of 500 draws (see the intervals of Fig. 6).

page.lede: Blagus and Lusa ran their simulations and the breast cancer analysis in R and published them in 2010 without the code. In November 2026 we rebuilt both from the paper (an R package, multds, with the nine classifiers, the three corrections and the measures) and reran the settings the figures and tables need, except MultDS for RF, SVM and PAM (and, with centred variables, for six classifiers), which our compute budget left out. Of {items} results, {exact} are exact, {agrees} agree, {partly} partly agree, {differs} differ and {not_attempted} were not attempted. Every gap has a cause; {open_causes} stay open, chiefly the SVM's and PAM's unstated settings, the sample centring of the p = 40 panels, RF-THR in the null case and the tails of a few prediction intervals.
page.tables_caption: Every cell of the four tables in the additional files: the simulations of Additional files 1 and 3 and the breast cancer tables 13 and 14.
page.items_caption: Each result of the paper, with the verdict computed from results.json and, for each one that is not exact, why.
page.claims_line: The main conclusions hold in our run: the classifiers are biased towards the majority class, variable selection adds to the bias, over-sampling helps little for most classifiers, and down-sizing and above all multiple down-sizing remove most of the bias, on the simulations and the breast cancer data. The claims that miss come from the SVM, PAM after over-sampling, RF-THR in the null case, selection at k1train 0.9 and a few interval ends.
came_back: Figs 1 and 2: every classifier except the SVM and, near balance, PAM came back within Monte Carlo error at p = 40, 1000 and 10000 ({fig1_hits} of {fig1_n} and {fig2_hits} of {fig2_n} points).

Down-sizing and MultDS (Fig. 5, Additional files 8 and 10) came back point by point for every classifier we ran except the SVM; Additional file 10's intervals match a 20-sample test set ({af10_hits} of {af10_n} ends), not the 500 its caption says.
RF-THR and PLR-THR (Additional file 11): {af11_hits} of {af11_n} points.

The Sotiriou arrays came back from the NCI archive: 99 tumours, 7650 probes, 34 ER- and 65 ER+. Fig. 6 came back {fig6_hits} of {fig6_n} means; Additional file 14 (MultDS) {af14_hits} of {af14_n} cells.
DLDA and DQDA are sma's stat.diag.da; our versions give identical predictions, and our AUC equals Hmisc's.
buried: The R scripts. The paper names the packages and released no code; no copy was found.
The SVM's cost and the direction of its class weights. No single setting fits the simulations and the breast cancer tables at once.
PAM's tie rule for the threshold. Our PAM is a little more biased near balance and at 45 ER+ / 5 ER-; neither the smallest tied threshold, cross-validation nor equal priors fits both.
The seeds. A few prediction-interval ends, set by the 13 lowest of 500 draws, land two steps of 0.05 from the paper's.
page.matched_intro: What the paper does not say, what it says that its figures contradict, and what we chose. Each was tested against the paper's own values.
matched: Stated for every setting, but Fig. 3's p = 40 and pDE = p points come back almost all without it (see the cause of Fig. 3); Additional files 4 and 5 fit much better without it too, though not fully.

The paper's DLDA and DQDA are fitted better by selection on the original training set, and its PAM by keeping the original class prior after over-sampling (tested at one or two k1train values, 200 replicates). Our run follows the Methods (selection on the over-sampled set, pamr's default prior).
Its over-sampling PA is that of a test set as imbalanced as the training set; Additional file 8, the same panel for all nine classifiers, uses a balanced one.
Ranked by the ratio of the two discriminants, not their difference: found by search; the predictions are the same.
Prints PLR's PA1, PA2 and PV1 for all nine classifiers; those cells are listed as paper slips and the rest compared.

The printed precision plus a Bonferroni multiple of the combined Monte Carlo standard error: our SD over our replicate count, plus the paper's SD (ours where it prints none) over the paper's replicate count.
page.closing: Blagus and Lusa, 2010. The simulations and the breast cancer analysis came back in November 2026, from the paper alone.
